title: NameOrigin Canonical Name Entity
description: Permanent canonical contract for a single given-name entity. Organizes knowledge into logical domains instead of the current flat, per-dataset field layout (see audit/knowledge-domains.json for the field-by-field migration mapping and audit/dataset-mapping.json for how today's data files feed each domain). This schema is architecture-only: it defines the target shape, not an implementation, migration order, or generator change. Every property carries custom `x-*` annotations (a standard JSON Schema extension convention) answering: is this researched or computed, is it user-visible, does it affect SEO, does it affect structured data (schema.org/JSON-LD), and whether multiple values are allowed.

identity.description: Domain: the entity's stable identifying facts. Always present; never null as a whole object.

slug.description: URL-safe canonical slug, deterministically derived from name.

name.description: Canonical display spelling of the name.

gender.description: Gender association as catalogued (not a claim about any individual bearer).

firstLetter.description: First character of `name`, for alphabetical browsing.

classification.description: Domain: style/thematic tags used for browsing and filtering. Distinct from `identity` because tags are assigned, not inherent.

categories.description: Assigned category tags (e.g. traditional, biblical, rare). See audit/knowledge-redundancy.json for the categories-vs-styles taxonomy overlap.

styleTags.description: Style-page taxonomy membership (modern, classic, nature, ...) — a separate, currently only partially-overlapping vocabulary from categories.

meaning.description: Domain: what the name means. Null (the whole object) is the canonical way to represent 'no researched meaning exists' — the model has no separate 'unknown' sentinel value; absence is absence. This directly replaces today's practice of substituting literal fallback text ('a documented given name') when this field is empty (see audit/fallback-taxonomy.json, mechanism meaning-fallback-documented-given-name).

alternates.description: Additional documented meanings where more than one tradition ascribes a different meaning.

confidence.description: Researcher confidence in `primary`, mirroring the existing origin_confidence pattern.

origin.description: Domain: geographic/cultural origin. Today this single concept is split across two files read by two different generators (data/names-enriched.json for most templates, data/names.json for the sibling-harmony generator) — see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json. The canonical model has exactly one origin object per entity, ending that split by construction.

cluster.description: Broader origin cluster (e.g. Indian, Nordic, Semitic) used for grouping/related-name logic.

confidence.description: Researcher confidence in the origin assignment.

language.description: Domain: linguistic association, kept distinct from `origin` (a name can be linguistically Sanskrit while its country of origin is catalogued as India — today these are two fields on one flat record; here they remain two fields but under a schema that makes the relationship explicit).

etymology.description: Domain: not present in any current dataset (a future expansion named explicitly in the Phase 2A brief). Placeholder structure only.

rootWord.description: The word(s) the name derives from.

rootLanguage.description: Language of the root word, which may differ from `language.primary` after linguistic evolution.

derivationNotes.description: Free-text account of how the name evolved from its root.

history.description: Domain: not present in any current dataset. Today's 'Historical and Cultural Context' section (buildCulturalContext()) renders unconditionally with generic substitute text when no real history exists (see audit/fallback-taxonomy.json, mechanism origin-fallback-various-cultural-traditions) — this domain is where a real, entity-specific historical record would live instead.

notableBearers.description: Notable historical or contemporary bearers of the name.

historicalUsageNotes.description: Free-text account of how usage has changed over time.

culture.description: Domain: cultural significance distinct from raw historical facts (history is 'what happened'; culture is 'what it means to people now').

religion.description: Domain: explicitly not present anywhere in the current project. Phase 1A's entity-map.json already recorded this absence directly ('No religion taxonomy exists in the dataset... the closest concept is the "biblical" value inside the categories.json taxonomy'). This domain formalizes where a real religion/tradition association would live, separate from the categories.json 'biblical' style tag it would eventually supersede for that purpose.

tradition.description: Associated religious tradition, if any (e.g. Christian, Islamic, Hindu, Jewish, secular).

scripturalReference.description: Reference to a scriptural or religious text where the name appears, if applicable.

usage.description: Domain: how and where the name is actually used today, as distinct from where it originated.

regionsOfUse.description: Countries/regions where the name sees notable current use (derived from `popularity.records`, not independently researched).

pronunciation.description: Domain: how the name sounds. Currently the single most under-populated domain in the live site — the backing `phonetic` field has 0% coverage across all 3,697 names (audit/knowledge-coverage.json), so the existing Pronunciation section has never rendered on any page.

audioUrl.description: Optional pronunciation audio clip — a genuinely new capability, not present in any current dataset.

variants.description: Domain: alternate spellings. Today represented in two separate datasets (data/variants.json and data/normalized-names.json's spelling_variants[]) that were not verified to be identical — see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json.

spellingVariants.description: Alternate spellings, each optionally tagged with a language.

transliterations.description: Renderings in non-Latin scripts (e.g. Devanagari, Cyrillic, Arabic) — a future expansion named explicitly in the Phase 2A brief; not present in any current dataset.

nicknames.description: Domain: not present in any current dataset. Distinct from `variants` (a variant is an alternate FORM of the same name; a nickname is a shortened/affectionate name derived from it, e.g. 'Liam' from 'William').

relatedNames.description: Domain: this name's place in the wider name graph. `equivalents` is today's closed, curated data/name-equivalents.json set; `similarNames` and `clusterId` correspond to the algorithmic 'Names Like X' and topic-cluster mechanisms.

similarNameIds.description: Algorithmically-similar names (phonetic/origin/popularity/gender pools), i.e. today's Names Like X page contents.

popularity.description: Domain: usage-frequency data over time and geography. Currently the second-sparsest domain (0.14% entity-level coverage) and additionally fragmented across three datasets (data/popularity.json, data/country-differentials.json, data/regional-trend-acceleration.json) that each derive overlapping-but-not-identical metrics from the same underlying source — see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json.

trendAcceleration.description: (rank_earlier - rank_later) / years, positive = rising — the metric data/regional-trend-acceleration.json computes today.

relationships.description: Domain: this name's computed relationships to OTHER entities (surnames, sibling names, comparison pairs) — distinct from relatedNames, which is about other first names sharing this name's own attributes. Note: surname_compatibility and comparisonPairs reference a Surname Entity and a Country Entity respectively, neither of which is defined by this Name Entity schema (see docs/CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md, 'Domain boundaries', and audit/schema-validation.json for the explicit unmapped-scope note).

surnameCompatibility.description: Computed first+last name phonetic compatibility scores.

siblingPairs.description: Computed sibling-name harmony scores. sharedOrigin is nullable because today's sibling generator reads unenriched data — see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json.

citations.description: Domain: provenance for every researched (non-computed) fact above — a future expansion named explicitly in the Phase 2A brief; not present in any current dataset. Today's 'Sources and Etymology' section (buildReferenceBlock()) renders a generic, non-entity-specific list of source CATEGORIES on every page regardless of whether any real citation exists for that entity.

field.description: Which domain/field this citation supports, e.g. 'meaning.primary'.

metadata.description: Domain: record-keeping about the entity itself, not about the name. Always present.

dataCompletenessScore.description: Fraction of non-null leaf fields across the whole entity — a diagnostic figure, not a quality judgment.
